title: Tool Selection Quality on Agent LLM Spans
dataSources: Tool Selection Quality results on sampled LLM spans; requires the `tools` schemas on each LLM span
description: Scores whether the agent picked the right tool with the right arguments for each request, including turns where no tool should have been called, using the Tool Selection Quality evaluator on LLM spans in Splunk Agent Observability.
value: Wrong tool choices cause wrong answers and unwanted side effects, such as a write tool run on a plain question. Scoring them on live traffic shows which prompts or tool descriptions need work.
implementation: Log `tools=` (the function schemas offered) on every LLM span, then turn on Tool Selection Quality for the Agent Stream with an explicit sample rate. Review traces scored wrong. An evaluator scores traces that are already stored and never blocks the reply. To stop or redirect a step inline, use Agent Control (UC-13.8.26).
visualization: Tool Selection Quality column in the trace table; rationale per scored span.
knownFalsePositives: It judges the tool against the request, not the tool alone: the same write tool can score correct on a change request and wrong on a question. It does not judge scope: an out-of-scope request that ran a plausible read tool can score correct.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`. Pass the tool definitions in `tools`, not the call the model made; the logger reference docstring has shown a tool call in that example.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Evaluators are defined for the organization and turned on per Agent Stream, in the console (Configure Evaluators) or with `enable_evaluators`. That SDK call replaces the stream's set: anything left out is turned off. Evaluators run after the trace is stored, on a sample. A 10% rate stores every trace and scores one in ten, and a sampled trace is scored by every enabled evaluator. There is no documented default sample rate, so set it explicitly. Preset judges are LLM-as-a-judge: several votes, majority or average, plus a rationale.

Step 3 — Validate

With the evaluator on, the stream's `get_metrics()` returns `['tool_selection_quality']`; use it to check what is on without changing anything. In query results the score is keyed by the evaluator's UUID: `metrics_<uuid>` holds the judge votes, with `_rationale`, `_num_judges` and `_status` alongside. In field testing, scores for new traces appeared within 2 minutes and traces already in the stream were scored too. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Review traces scored wrong each week with the prompt owner. For a clean-versus-faulty comparison, pick a question that goes through the tool loop in both runs. Add an alert on the score with UC-13.8.24.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Spans show not applicable: the LLM span has no `tools` (see UC-13.8.14). The evaluator reports a missing integration: that is the org's model integration, not the agent code.
grandmaExplanation: A reviewer checks whether the assistant reached for the right tool for each question, like checking a plumber brought a wrench and not a hammer.

productArtifacts.title: Tool Selection Quality evaluator
productArtifacts.body:
Where: Agent Stream > Configure Evaluators (or enable_evaluators in the SDK)
Evaluator: Tool Selection Quality
Judge: LLM-as-a-judge, yes/no by consensus of several votes
Scores: LLM spans; correct when the tool and arguments match the request, and when no tool was appropriate
Sample rate: set explicitly for the stream; there is no documented default
Notes: Pass tools= (the schemas) on each LLM span or the span is marked not applicable.
